fence_points.what: parse_silver_key takes the master from the folder segment, so a firm folder would be read as a master named by the folder.
head_set admits a closure object by folder-prefix startswith over data_prefixes, with no file-name test.
list_dates turns every key under the completion prefix into one per-master date set with no file-name check.
_prefixes_of turns each source's one-level listing into scopes, so a shared folder becomes one scope for every master beneath it.
IAM s3:prefix glob over source/*/silver/ admits every master folder under a source; IAM cannot fence by file name.

dual_read_notes: Account list (integration.py:364-396) reads the snapshot for the requested business date (integration.py:665), not a newest-partition lookup, so its dual read is the catalog's: silver entries name the file-name form first and the old data.parquet form second.

Files list and query (integration.py:505 and :641) take objects from catalog.snapshot, which builds keys at catalog.py:336 and admits them by folder prefix at catalog.py:603 and :628; the change is in canonical_object_key and parse_silver_key (catalog.py:545-550), and a fallback is safe only if a missing new object is treated as absent, never as a changed source.

Fetch (integration.py:203-220) refuses any key outside data_prefixes and then GETs the pinned VersionId with the same role and bucket; silver stays in opal-data-assets, so the fallback is between pinned versions, not between buckets.

Completion listing and marker read (catalog.py:779-804 and :993-997) CANNOT be a simple fallback: the state tier is in another bucket and a dated name (date=D then the master file), the tail parse at catalog.py:798-800 would skip that form silently, and the contract carries one source_bucket and one CATALOG role.

family_depth backfill status (family_depth.py:215-225 and :298-306) CANNOT be a simple fallback: the key is a fixed suffix joined to a discovered scope in the monolith bucket, while the new rolling object needs a LIST for the newest dated partition at or before today in the state bucket and then a GET.
Scope discovery (family_depth.py:228-245) would list a shared firm folder as one scope, so the fence there must be by file name and cannot come from the listing alone.
Catalog rows (DATA_CATALOG.yaml) feed the client surface (client_core.py:221-227), which refuses the 0840 master at mint (client_adapter_schwab.py:175); no dual read is needed for those rows.

No gateway code path reads the relayed last_run, conversions, pulls, daily_pull or _ops names, so nothing is dual-read for them; bronze has one reader (catalog.py:456-459, the closure partition check) and the relay names no bronze destination, so its edit is open and filed as a surprise row. IAM: the data and catalog roles deny every bucket but opal-data-assets (schwab_reader_iam.tf:194-198 and :261-265) and deny prefixes outside their lists, so the new silver and state grants are the named widening and the family_depth glob at family_depth_read_iam.tf:64 cannot fence by file name.
